newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says willing to cancel Rwanda arms deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says willing to cancel Rwanda arms deal.

text.p: South Africa will cancel its 87 million rand ($18.5 million) arms deal with Rwanda if asked to do so by leaders in the region after a summit on Tuesday, a senior minister said.

Cabinet minister Kader Asmal, chairman of the National Conventional Arms Control Committee (NCACC) that sanctions weapons exports, told reporters that South Africa would be guided by leaders of the Great Lakes states surrounding Rwanda and Zaire.
"We will follow the advice of the Great Lakes region," Asmal said.

He said his arms control committee was scheduled to meet on November 14, but that he and Defence Minister Joe Modise could cancel or suspend the contract if this was deemed to be in the national interest.
Asmal said South Africa had so far delivered only armoured personnel carriers to the Rwandan government.

East and Central African leaders are scheduled to meet in Nairobi on Tuesday to discuss the worsening situation in eastern Zaire, where ethnic Tutsi rebels, with the support of the Rwandan army, have are fighting Zairean government troops.
